package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware distributed as ELF binaries and shell scripts, not via a package manager)
package_info.package_versions: N/A (affects all versions as it is not a package in the traditional sense)
package_info.why_malicious: Shikitega is a multi-stage Linux malware that leverages polymorphic encoding to evade detection, delivers a Metasploit meterpreter for remote control, exploits privilege escalation vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-3493, CVE-2021-4034), establishes persistence via unauthorized cron job creation, and installs a cryptominer. It abuses legitimate cloud services for command and control, providing attackers with full remote access, persistence, and illicit cryptomining capabilities. Its entire operation is malicious, with no legitimate use case.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Polymorphically encoded shellcode that downloads and executes the Metasploit 'Mettle' meterpreter payload from a remote C2 server.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At initial execution, the code decodes itself in memory, initiates a network connection to a remote C2 server, downloads the Metasploit meterpreter payload, writes it to disk, and executes it, resulting in remote shell access for the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Self-decoding shellcode that downloads and executes a remote payload is a hallmark of malware loaders and is rarely, if ever, found in legitimate software.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal binaries do not contain polymorphic shellcode that fetches and executes remote code without user interaction.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Polymorphic encoding may be used in security research or CTF challenges, but not in production or user-facing software.

execution_context.file_location: meterpreter payload (downloaded and executed by dropper)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Metasploit 'Mettle' meterpreter binary, which provides a remote shell and command execution capabilities.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After being executed by the dropper, the code establishes a reverse shell connection to the attacker's C2 server, receives and executes arbitrary commands, and enables full remote control of the infected system.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Meterpreter is a well-known post-exploitation tool used by attackers to maintain remote access and control over compromised systems.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not install or execute remote access trojans or provide unauthorized remote shell access.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Penetration testers may use meterpreter in authorized red team engagements, but never in production environments without explicit consent.
key_indicators: Reverse shell connection to external C2

execution_context.file_location: exploit modules within the dropper or downloaded components

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Exploit code targeting CVE-2021-3493 (overlayfs privilege escalation) and CVE-2021-4034 (Polkit pkexec privilege escalation) to gain root access.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After initial access, the code executes local privilege escalation exploits targeting CVE-2021-3493 and CVE-2021-4034, manipulates system processes and files to obtain root privileges, and enables further persistence and payload installation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Automated exploitation of local vulnerabilities for privilege escalation is a common malware tactic to gain unauthorized root access.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not exploit local vulnerabilities to escalate privileges or gain root access without user knowledge.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Security tools may test for vulnerabilities, but do not exploit them for persistence or privilege escalation in production systems.
key_indicators: Inclusion of public exploit code for known CVEs

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After gaining root privileges, the code writes a new cron job entry to /etc/crontab, scheduling the cryptominer binary to execute every minute, thereby establishing persistence for the malicious payload.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Malware commonly uses cron jobs for persistence, especially to ensure continuous execution of cryptominers or other payloads.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software rarely installs persistent cron jobs as root without explicit user consent or administrative oversight.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: System administrators may use cron for scheduled tasks, but not for hidden or unauthorized cryptominer execution.
key_indicators: Frequent execution of unknown binaries as root

execution_context.file_location: downloaded cryptominer binary (location set by cron job)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Downloaded and executed XMRig or similar Monero cryptominer binary.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When triggered by the cron job, the code executes the cryptominer binary, initiates outbound connections to Monero mining pools, and consumes system CPU resources to mine cryptocurrency for the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unsolicited cryptominer installation and execution is a clear sign of system compromise and resource abuse.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not install or run cryptominers without explicit user consent and configuration.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Cryptomining is legitimate only when explicitly installed and configured by the system owner for their own benefit.
key_indicators: Outbound connections to Monero mining pools
Abnormal or sustained high CPU usage

execution_context.file_location: all malware components (dropper, shell scripts, binaries)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Polymorphic encoder/obfuscator applied to all malware modules, changing the binary signature on each infection.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At every stage, the code applies a polymorphic encoder to obfuscate its own binary and script components, alters the binary signature on each infection, and hinders static detection by antivirus engines.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Polymorphic encoding is a classic malware evasion technique designed to bypass signature-based detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not self-modify or obfuscate its code in a way that changes its binary signature on each execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Obfuscation may be used for DRM or intellectual property protection, but not for malware delivery or evasion.
key_indicators: Self-modifying code in ELF binaries and scripts
Frequent changes in binary signature across infections
Obfuscation of payloads and loader routines

attack_chain.action: Initial execution of the Shikitega dropper, which uses polymorphic encoding to evade detection.
attack_chain.leads_to: Download and execution of the meterpreter payload

attack_chain.action: Download and execution of the Metasploit meterpreter, providing remote shell access.
Exploit local Linux vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-3493, CVE-2021-4034) to escalate privileges to root.
Establish persistence by writing a cron job as root to execute the cryptominer.
Download and execute the cryptominer, which connects to a mining pool and uses system resources.

behavioral_signatures: Polymorphic/self-modifying code in ELF binaries and shell scripts
Initial payload downloads and executes remote code (meterpreter)
Automated exploitation of local privilege escalation vulnerabilities (CVE-2021-3493, CVE-2021-4034)
Unauthorized creation or modification of root cron jobs in /etc/crontab or /etc/cron.*
Silent installation and execution of cryptominer binaries (e.g., XMRig) in non-standard locations
file_indicators: Unknown ELF binaries with polymorphic encoding
New or modified entries in /etc/crontab or /etc/cron.*
Cryptominer binaries (e.g., XMRig) in unusual locations
network_indicators: Reverse shell connections initiated by meterpreter
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for unknown or obfuscated ELF binaries and shell scripts executing on Linux systems, especially those that download and execute remote payloads. Watch for exploitation attempts targeting CVE-2021-3493 and CVE-2021-4034. Audit /etc/crontab and /etc/cron.* for unauthorized entries, particularly those running unknown binaries as root. Detect outbound connections to known C2 domains (dash.cloudflare.ovh, main.cloudfronts.net) and Monero mining pools. Use file integrity monitoring to detect new or modified binaries and scripts with known malicious hashes. Correlate high CPU usage with the presence of cryptominer binaries to identify illicit mining activity.
